name: Apollo, Dionysus and Daphne
description: The composed philosophical whole: a world becomes a view, the view grows confident, Dionysus opens the enclosure, participation risks its own overriding image, Daphne requires someone to remain other, the view becomes transparent to its context, and form returns with its source still able to answer.

text.kicker: #0 · the authored whole; Nietzsche and Gebser in distinct registers
text.title: A world becomes a view
text.italic: Apollo embodies form's gift: the image lets one person show another what has been seen, and gives the seer something definite to revisit and change.

text.body: A finite being gives the world a form it can inhabit and communicate: something stands out, a boundary makes it distinct, an image holds it long enough to become intelligible. Apollo names this achievement — showing another what has been seen without occupying the same place, and giving the seer something definite to revisit, question and change. This is Taylor's composed whole; the sequence lives in seeing, participating and answering.
Occurrences: the standing-out and its boundary (#0); the communicable image (#0, #1); the revisitable view (#0, #5→0).

text.kicker: #1 · Gebser pp.11–21, 255–58 (paraphrased); Taylor's P5 carrier; A20
text.title: The view grows confident of its own completeness
text.italic: Possession begins when the image's valuation governs what its source is allowed to be — the aloof neutrality presents situated authority as though its conditions had vanished.

text.body: The movement begins when formation grows confident: the view conceals the life from which it was selected, then treats whatever escapes its measure as deficient. Gebser gives perspectivity its achievement — Giotto's depth, Petrarch's landscape, Alberti's construction — and its restriction when one sector claims exclusive validity. Taylor's P5 carrier brings the pressure inside the viewer: body, history,

language and concern affect what becomes salient. The absent Father gives concealment its authorial image — lack numbed, a surrogate invoked as ultimate warrant while the view's own position exempts itself from the order it imposes. A20 receives the transition: possession occurs when the image's valuation governs what its source is allowed to be; the difference appears when the source resists.

text.kicker: #2 · Nietzsche Birth of Tragedy §1 (p.21) and §21 (p.167); the central plan's dismemberment
text.title: Dionysus opens the enclosure and returns through form
text.italic: Dionysus names the release through which the view's implication in life becomes available again — within this composition, what dies is the form's claim, and what returns must be communicable enough to answer for.

text.body: Participation restores the view to the living relation its self-sufficiency concealed. The central plan gives this release the force of dismemberment and death/rebirth: within this Taylor-authored sequence, what dies is the form's claim to stand complete in itself; what returns must acquire a form through which living relation can continue. Nietzsche supplies the artistic relation: in §1, art develops through the duplexity of the Apollonian

and Dionysian; in §21, Dionysus speaks Apollo's language and Apollo finally speaks Dionysus's. The formed account must let its participation affect what it says; participation must become communicable enough for a particular speaker to answer for it. Yet openness does not settle the question: participation can itself become an overriding image — unity deciding in advance what another being's difference must mean.

scenes.character: Apollo cannot make illumination into entitlement; Dionysus cannot make participation into permission to absorb. Her alterity requires both powers to return differently.

entities.name: Daphne — the centre that exceeds what either power makes of her
the transformed tree's recoil — preserved with the seeming assent
Apollo — articulation without final possession

text.kicker: #3 · the alterity check (human-amplified: yes); the Ovidian whole kept distinct
text.title: Daphne requires someone to remain other
text.italic: Daphne proves-discloses the difference between failures: appropriation through determination and appropriation through undifferentiation — her separate literary whole bears its own cast, pursuit, transformation and afterlife.

text.body: Daphne changes what the mutuality must accomplish: a relation can be vivid and shared while still failing to let the other answer in their own right. Apollo cannot make illumination into entitlement; Dionysus cannot make participation permission to absorb. Her office is the particular centre whose existence exceeds what either power makes of it.

Her separate literary whole is Ovid's; the movement-35 return keeps the tree's recoil with the narrator's seeming assent, so no easy union or final refusal replaces it. Appropriation after withdrawal: possession failing at one level need not end the image's symbolic continuation. Unity invoked to cancel refusal repeats appropriation by other means. Occurrences: her required otherness (#3); recoil with seeming assent (Mv 35); Dionysus enters through Taylor, not Ovid.

text.title: The view becomes transparent to its context
text.italic: The diaphanous form embodies determination visible together with the conditions through which it became a view — promising no exhaustive panorama.

text.body: The resulting form is diaphanous: its determination remains visible together with the conditions through which it has become a view. Gebser's aperspectivity releases perspective from exclusive validity without amalgamating earlier structures; his Picasso/Braque discussion makes time and multiple aspects material to representation. Q27's contextual-field programme gives the movement its 180°→360° expression: the perspectival triangle opens

into a field where positions, counter-positions and transitions are available together — and the knower has a position within that field. Wider collections cannot accomplish this by accumulation; limits, relations and means of transformation have to become intelligible. P5's concern gives transparency a lived direction: equanimity requires acknowledging concern; the pose of having no stake can conceal a governing preference.

text.kicker: #5→0 · A20/A21; Movement 35; Draft 3; the shared Neumann ground
text.title: Form returns with its source still able to answer
text.italic: What returns is a form capable of being changed by the world it discloses — the sequence closes in another finite act of seeing, where the other's answer remains their own.

text.body: The shared Neumann whole grounds the declared A20/A21 relation through differentiation, the image's power and transformed recognition; the composed whole gives that structuration its form–participation–alterity movement. Apollo returns to articulation — a definite image again offered, now bearing an acknowledged relation to the life it expresses and the difference it cannot appropriate. Dionysus remains effective within its communicability; Daphne remains

effective within that participation — another centre can answer without being pre-assigned the answer completing the speaker's image. Draft 3: truth beyond any frame, truth through this particular angle and life; a form once opened can close again, and renewed encounter must affect its valuation. Declared cross-story: Daphne ↔ the Apollo/Dionysus bracket — distinct casts. Occurrences: renewed finite seeing (#0, #5→0); the answer remaining the other's own (#3, #5→0).
